intro: A full scale of certainty, from sure to doubtful, with the phrases for what you have heard, what you have realised and what you do not care about.
p.estar convencido de que.consejo: It takes «de que» and the indicative: «estoy convencido de que viene». For a woman: «convencida».
p.estar seguro de que.consejo: Do not forget «de»: «estoy seguro de que». Leaving it out is a very common mistake.
p.no cabe duda de que.consejo: It is formal. «Cabe» comes from «caber». The indicative follows: «no cabe duda de que es difícil».
p.sin duda.consejo: It goes at the start or in the middle of the sentence: «sin duda, tienes razón». The d in «duda» is a normal d.
p.lo más probable es que.consejo: It takes the subjunctive: «lo más probable es que llueva». «Probable» ends in -ble.
p.igual.consejo: In Spain, «igual viene» means «maybe he is coming». With this «igual» the indicative is used.
p.tengo entendido que.consejo: It presents what you have heard without swearing to it. The indicative follows: «tengo entendido que se ha jubilado».
p.por lo visto.consejo: It is used to report something you heard or saw from afar. It is similar to «al parecer».
p.al parecer.consejo: It goes at the start: «al parecer, no vendrá». «Al» and «parecer» are written separately.
p.darse cuenta de que.consejo: It is pronominal and takes «de que»: «me doy cuenta de que falta algo». You do not say «me doy cuenta que».
p.me da lo mismo.glosa: it is all the same to me
p.me da lo mismo.consejo: It is the same as «me da igual». If the subject changes, the subjunctive follows: «me da lo mismo que venga».
p.qué más da.consejo: It is a rhetorical question: it expects no answer. «Qué» is written with an accent.
p.dudar de que.consejo: It asks for the subjunctive: «dudo de que venga». If you have no doubt, the indicative: «no dudo de que viene».
p.no tener ni idea.consejo: It is colloquial. It is shortened to «ni idea». The «ni» reinforces the negation.
b1.texto:
**Sure.** With the indicative:

- **Estoy seguro de que** viene.
- **Estoy convencido de que** tiene razón.
- **No cabe duda de que** es difícil.
- **Sin duda**, **por supuesto**.

Watch the **de**: estoy seguro **de que**, me doy cuenta **de que**. Leaving it out is a frequent mistake.

**Probable.** **Lo más probable es que venga.** (subjunctive)

**Possible.** **Igual viene.** In Spain, this «igual» takes the indicative.

**Doubtful.** **Dudo de que venga.** **No estoy seguro de que venga.** If you deny certainty, the subjunctive comes in.

**Second-hand.** **Tengo entendido que** se ha jubilado. **Por lo visto**, se han separado. **Al parecer**…

**Not knowing, not caring.** **No tengo ni idea.** **Me da lo mismo.** **¿Qué más da?**
b2.f0.texto: Do you know if Rebeca is coming to the dinner?
b2.f1.texto: As I understand it she is away.
b2.f3.texto: Apparently she has fallen out with Julio.
b2.f4.texto: Most probably she will not come.
b2.f5.texto: Well, I am convinced she is coming.
b2.f7.texto: I realise she has not answered the message.
b2.f9.texto: It is all the same to me.
b4.titulo: Indicative or subjunctive depending on certainty
b4.texto:
The mood of the verb depends on how much certainty you express:

- **Certainty** + indicative: **estoy seguro de que viene**, **no cabe duda de que es difícil**.
- **Probability** + subjunctive: **lo más probable es que venga**.
- **Doubt** + subjunctive: **dudo de que venga**, **no estoy seguro de que venga**.
- **Igual** (maybe) + indicative: **igual viene**.

Do not forget the preposition: **estoy seguro de que**, **me doy cuenta de que**. For what does not matter: **me da lo mismo**; with another subject, the subjunctive: **me da lo mismo que venga**.
b4.e0.texto: I am sure he is coming.
b4.e2.texto: There is no doubt that it is difficult.
b5.f0.texto: The table is laid for eight people and smells of lemon and bay leaf.
b5.f1.texto: Elsa places the napkins carefully and lines up the glasses one by one.
b5.f2.texto: A small candle trembles in the centre of the table.
b5.f3.texto: In the kitchen, the soup simmers over a low heat with a steady murmur.
b5.f4.texto: Elsa looks at the clock on the wall and feels no hurry at all.
b5.f5.texto: At nine the doorbell rings with two short rings.
b5.f6.texto: In the corridor you can hear laughter, footsteps and the rustle of coats.
b5.f7.texto: Rebeca appears at the door with red cheeks and a bottle in her hand.
b5.f8.texto: Elsa smiles, because she has no doubts left.
b5.f9.texto: Mario raises his eyebrows with a smile of victory.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «estar seguro de que» always takes «de».
b6.o1.refuerzo: The preposition «de» is missing: a frequent mistake.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The «que» that joins both parts is missing.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it warns that you do not know it first-hand.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That expression says you are completely sure.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That says something does not matter to you.
b7.pregunta: Which expression reports something you have only heard?
b8.frase: Lo más probable es que no ____.
b8.o0.refuerzo: It is indicative; «lo más probable es que» asks for the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: The future does not follow «es que» here.
b9.frase: A mí me da lo mismo
b9.traduccion: It is all the same to me
b10.o1: No cabe duda de que viene.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «dudar de que» plus the subjunctive.
b10.pregunta: Which of these sentences expresses doubt?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I have no idea.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: this colloquial «igual» takes the indicative.
b12.o1.refuerzo: With «igual» the subjunctive is not used.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The imperfect subjunctive does not go here.
p.vuelto.consejo: With «ha», it forms the perfect: «ha vuelto», has come back.
p.dudo.consejo: «dudar de que» is followed by the subjunctive: «dudo de que venga».
p.difícil.consejo: The accent on í shows the stress. Its opposite is «fácil».
p.puesta.consejo: «estar puesta» describes a table already set. It agrees with «mesa».
p.laurel.consejo: A leaf used to flavour soups and stews.
p.alinea.consejo: «alinear» means to put things in a straight line.
p.hierve.consejo: «hervir» changes e to ie. The h is silent and the v sounds like b.
p.cortos.consejo: Its opposite is «largos», long. It agrees with «golpes».
p.oyen.consejo: «oír» means to hear without trying. The y sounds like «y».
p.roce.consejo: From «rozar», to brush against. The c sounds like th.
